title: Assessing the effect of therapeutic level of oxytetracycline dihydrate on pharmacokinetics and biosafety in Oncorhynchus

predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The paper writes AUC = Σ (C_i + C_{i+1})·(t_{i+1} − t_i). The trapezoidal rule requires a factor of ½: AUC = ½ Σ (C_i + C_{i+1})·(t_{i+1} − t_i). As written the formula overestimates all AUC values by exactly a factor of 2, invalidating all reported AUC(0–128) values.

predicted_errors.error_location: Results, Pharmacokinetic result (half-lives vs elimination rate constant)
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The text states the elimination rate constant was highest in gill at 0.01 h⁻¹, yet also reports the gill half-life as 0.94 h. Using the paper's own relation t½ = ln(2)/k, k = 0.01 h⁻¹ gives t½ ≈ 69 h, not 0.94 h (0.94 h implies k ≈ 0.74 h⁻¹). The reported rate constants and half-lives for the tissues are mutually inconsistent (liver 5.75 h → k = 0.12 h⁻¹, kidney 13.12 h → 0.053 h⁻¹, all far above the stated 'highest' 0.01 h⁻¹).

predicted_errors.error_location: Abstract and Results (absorption rate constants vs Tmax)
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Reported Ka values of 0.0002–0.011 h⁻¹ correspond (via the paper's Ka = ln2/t½a) to absorption half-lives of ~63 h to ~3466 h, which is incompatible with the reported Tmax values of 3 h (gill), 16 h (liver, skin), 24 h (plasma) and 32 h (kidney, muscle). A plasma Ka of 0.0002 h⁻¹ cannot produce a plasma peak at 24 h.

The text claims an ascending ordering: 'the shortest half-life observed in the gill tissue (0.94 h), followed by the liver (5.75 h), kidney (13.12 h), skin (9.88 h), and muscle (17.23 h)'. Skin (9.88 h) is shorter than kidney (13.12 h), so the stated ordering contradicts the values given.

predicted_errors.error_location: Materials and methods – 'The preparation of medicated feed' vs 'Experimental fish'/dosing description
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The method first describes preparing oxytetracycline-coated medicated feed and starving fish before 'administration of the medicated feed', but then states the dose was given 'through gavaging in semi liquid form'. Oral gavage and voluntary consumption of medicated feed are distinct administration routes with different absorption kinetics; the described protocol is internally contradictory and the actual route is indeterminate.

predicted_errors.error_location: Methods 'The preparation of medicated feed' vs 'Experimental design – Preparation of medicated feed'
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The first description states the medicated feed 'was dried for a period of 30 min in the absence of light', while the biosafety section states 'the feed was dried in the dark for 1 h'. The same described procedure is given two different drying times without explanation.

The study states PK parameters were derived with 'a non-compartmental pharmacokinetic model grounded in statistical moment theory', yet reports an absorption rate constant (Ka), a distribution half-life (t½a) and a separate elimination half-life (t½b) with a 'biphasic pattern'. These are compartmental-model parameters that cannot be obtained from non-compartmental analysis.

predicted_errors.error_location: Results – liver elimination half-life (238.68 h) and elimination duration (606.33 h)
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Sampling ended at 128 h post-dose, yet an elimination half-life of 238.68 h and an elimination phase duration of 606.33 h are reported for liver. These values are extrapolated far beyond the observation window and cannot be supported by the data collected.

The described SPE procedure includes conditioning, sample loading and a wash with 0.5 mL acetonitrile:water, but no elution step or elution solvent is specified; nevertheless '2.5 mL of the eluent was collected'. As written the extraction cannot yield the stated eluate volume, and the retained analyte is never eluted.

predicted_errors.error_location: Methods – 'Validation and optimization of OTC using LC/MS/MS' (withdrawal time by WT 1.4)
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Withdrawal time was reportedly calculated with WT 1.4 (EMA linear-regression approach), which requires residue depletion data at several post-treatment time points. The biosafety sampling schedule (days 10, 20, 30, 40 with dosing through day 30) provides only a single post-dosing sampling point, which is insufficient for the stated calculation.

'The results were presented as mean ± SD (standard deviation of the mean)' conflates standard deviation with the standard error of the mean; these are different quantities, making the reported dispersion measure ambiguous.

The validation guideline cited is Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2021/808, not a 'Commission Decision 2021/808/EC'. The instrument type and designation are misattributed (Decision 2002/657/EC is the earlier document it replaced).

The abstract states 'The pharmacokinetics study spanned a duration of 5 days', but the sampling schedule extends to 128 h post-administration (≈5.3 days), plus a 12 h starvation and 15-day acclimatization period; the stated duration does not match the described protocol.

The text states the kidney concentration peaked at 9380 µg kg⁻¹ at 32 h, but in the same sentence says 'The absorption rate reduced after 16 h, and the concentration declined', implying a decline beginning before the stated Tmax. The narrative contradicts itself about when the kidney concentration began to fall.
